top_story.headline: Lobbying firm reports pushing White House and Justice Department on clemency for a client in a securities dispute
top_story.dek: A third-quarter Lobbying Disclosure Act report from Rulon & White Governance Strategies lists clemency work for Veriteaseum alongside Securities and Exchange Commission negotiations.
paragraphs: A 3rd Quarter report filed by Rulon & White Governance Strategies for its client Veritaseum Inc. describes the issue as: "Securities Exchange Commission Emmet and Murphy Negotiations U.S Senate Tim Scott Department of Justice Department of Clemency White House Counsel Alice Johnson Clemency for Reginald Middleton." The lobbyist listed is Todd White.

The text is quoted as filed. It names the White House Counsel, the Department of Justice and Alice Johnson in connection with clemency for Reginald Middleton, and it puts that work in the same entry as the securities negotiations. The report does not say whether any contact took place or what the outcome was.

The Pardon Lobbying section below carries the filing link. No other filing in today's window showed a communication with the President, the Vice President or a cabinet member. No new House financial disclosures turned up, and the Senate disclosure check failed, so Senate coverage is incomplete.

sections.headline: No new House filings in the window; Senate check failed
paragraphs: The input contained no House or Senate financial disclosures filed since October 30 that earlier editions had not already reported, so there are no trade reports to summarize. The Senate eFD fetch returned an error, so this is not a confirmation that no Senate filings were made.

sections.headline: Eight quarterly reports posted, no new registrations or terminations
paragraphs: Eight Lobbying Disclosure Act filings were posted since November 1: six 3rd Quarter reports reporting no activity and two 3rd Quarter reports with activity. There were no new registrations and no terminations, and none of the activity reports carried a signal such as covered former officials, foreign entities or conviction disclosures. The two notable activity reports are covered in the extras sections below.

blocks.text: Tracking 483 Senate-confirmed officials with ethics agreements since Jan. 20, 2025. Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.
